vibe.rationale: Vibe 5 — one-point upgrade from the three-session Vibe 4 hold (July 8 evening through July 10 evening). The session's analytical structure is dominated by three independent positive resolutions arriving in the same reporting cycle, against which the session's residual risk factors are significant but bounded. Positive factor 1 (US-Iran talks resuming): The Al Arabiya / Times of Israel confirmed resumption of US-Iran negotiations on July 11 — explicitly including nuclear talks — is the most significant MOU-operational development since the July 8 Trump 'ceasefire over' declaration at NATO Ankara. The Khamenei state funeral (6-day, July 3-9, burial July 9 in Mashhad) imposed a diplomatic pause on both sides that made the July 8-10 acute-stress framing partially ambiguous — Iran's non-response to the Qatar channel was partly structural (mourning protocols) rather than purely adversarial. The July 11 resumption re-establishes the dispute-resolution architecture as functional. The Doha communication channel agreed July 9-10 is the mechanism through which talks flow. Positive factor 2 (WTI below $72): WTI consolidating below $72 on July 11 is the first genuine normalization-zone pricing signal since the July 7-9 re-escalation sequence drove WTI to $75. The July 10 brief characterized the $73-74 pullback as 'de-risking from peak — not normalization.' The sub-$72 territory on July 11 is a different signal: Iran supply return is actively suppressing prices below the war-risk premium floor, which is what normalization pricing looks like. The directional signal has shifted from 'uncertainty premium retreating' to 'supply confidence emerging.' Positive factor 3 (Chelan Hills 95% + Kartar 100%): The Chelan Hills Fire's Day 7 ICS-209 at 95% contained (from 50% under red flag conditions on Day 6) is the most significant single containment breakthrough of the 2026 Washington fire season to date. The 200+ personnel held the dozer-line geometry through the red flag wind event exactly as the extended-containment posture required. Kartar Fire (Okanogan County) at 100% contained eliminates the session's highest-priority new fire from July 10. Together, these two containments reduce Washington's concurrent active large fire count from six toward four, and remove the highest-risk fire (Kartar, 15% containment under red flag) from the active threat matrix entirely. Residual risk factor 1 (Longview three-thread convergence T-0): The three-thread convergence is now open — Longview CSB elevated chemical vapor pressure risk window, FERC 30-day informational report T-7 (July 18), and measles sub-window peak closing tomorrow (July 12). The convergence has not triggered an incident; it is a risk concentration, not a crisis. But any Longview CSB event on July 11-18 would represent the brief's highest-consequence domestic infrastructure event at precisely the period when FERC's AI-grid reporting is active and the measles window is closing. Residual risk factor 2 (measles sub-window Day 3 peak): Day 3 of the high-consequence sub-window is the epidemiological peak for the June 19 Lumen Field exposure. Three consecutive clean days (July 9, 10, 11) in the peak window is the strongest reassurance signal of the entire measles arc. The window closes tomorrow (July 12, Day 10). Residual risk factor 3 (Russia CDU-11 confirmation): The CDU-10 + CDU-11 combined 75% offline confirmation materially extends the dual two-source inflationary shock timeline beyond the September FOMC horizon, complicating Warsh's deflationary impulse thesis. Residual risk factor 4 (B and O Fire new Okanogan): A new fire near Okanogan reported July 9 is not yet at large-fire scale but is inside the east Cascades onset region — any rapid growth warrants immediate tracking. Upgrade to Vibe 6 requires: US-Iran July 11 talks producing a scheduled direct technical nuclear timeline session (not just communication channel); WTI declining below $70 (genuine Lloyd's normalization territory); Chelan Hills Level 3 downgrade to Level 2 and Sourdough extended attack confirmed stable through Day 7; measles sub-window closing clean July 12; Longview July 11 elevated risk window proceeding without incident. Drop to Vibe 4 requires: US-Iran July 11 talks collapsing without output (Iran conditions walk back the communication channel); WTI rebounding above $74 on re-escalation signal; new large fire ignition in east Cascades onset zone July 11-12; Longview CSB chemical vapor event; measles King County cluster confirmed before sub-window closes.

items.summary: The July 11 session records the MOU's most significant operational positive since the July 8 'ceasefire over' declaration: US-Iran negotiations have resumed, confirmed by Al Arabiya and the Times of Israel, explicitly including nuclear talks. The resumption follows the end of Iran's 6-day state funeral for Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei (killed in a joint US-Israeli airstrike February 28, 2026; buried July 9 at the Shrine of Imam Reza in Mashhad). The analytical significance of the funeral-period context: the July 8-10 'acute stress' framing partly reflected a structural diplomatic pause imposed by mourning protocols rather than purely adversarial Iranian decision-making. Both sides' negotiators — including Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on the US side, and Iranian technical officials communicating through the Qatar/Pakistan mediator channel — were operating under the constraint of the 6-day national mourning period. The July 11 resumption re-establishes the dispute-resolution architecture agreed in Doha on July 9-10 as operational. The agenda for the July 11 session explicitly includes nuclear talks — the first confirmed nuclear-issue discussion since the MOU's 60-day compliance window opened June 19 — alongside the unresolved sanctions dispute (Iranian crude export waiver revoked July 7) and the $6B frozen assets question (not released in Doha; US retained leverage). The oil market's July 11 signal is the session's most commercially consequential data point independent of the diplomatic resumption: WTI has consolidated below $72 for the first time since the July 7-9 re-escalation sequence. The July 10 brief characterized the $73-74 pullback as 'de-risking from peak — not normalization.' The sub-$72 territory on July 11 has a different character: Iran's return supply flow into the Omani-corridor tanker stream is actively suppressing prices below the war-risk premium threshold that $74 represented. When WTI falls below the normalization floor because Iranian supply is arriving at buyers — not because the risk premium is politely retreating — that is the commercial gateway signal the brief has been tracking since June 19. The 60-day nuclear window is at Day 23 of 60, with approximately 38% elapsed and no formal nuclear technical timeline agreed. The formal MOU termination instruments remain absent: no SNSC formal void declaration confirmed, no CENTCOM naval blockade reinstatement order, no Kharg Island strike. The MOU is at Acute Stress Day 4 but with diplomatic engagement resumed and oil pricing in normalization territory.

items.summary: Five secondary geopolitical threads on July 11 evening. First: Russia fuel crisis Day 11 — the Omsk refinery's 75% capacity offline status is now confirmed by multiple industrial sources. The CDU-10 (crude distillation unit, 38% of Omsk's 440,000 bpd processing capacity) is classified as destroyed; the CDU-11 (37% of capacity) is halted due to supporting infrastructure damage incurred in the July 6 Ukrainian drone strike. Together, the two units account for approximately 75% of the Omsk refinery's total output — the world's largest oil refinery by single-site capacity. The Day 11 implication: the 'CDU-10 destroyed / CDU-11 potentially recoverable' framing from the July 10 brief understated the damage. With CDU-11 also offline, the Omsk restoration timeline is multi-month even in optimistic scenarios. Russia has imposed a diesel export ban through at least end of July to manage domestic supply. The Central Asian spillover is confirmed and expanding: Uzbekistan has cut flights due to jet fuel shortages at Tashkent and regional airports. Kazakhstan is importing fuel from China as supply insurance. The IEA's 'unprecedented' designation of the Russia fuel crisis is the operative analytical framework. For Warsh's September SEP deflationary impulse thesis: the dual two-source energy shock (Hormuz corridor war-risk premium + Russian domestic refining crisis) will not resolve before the September FOMC, even if both situations improve incrementally. The CDU-11 offline confirmation extends the Russian component's timeline substantially. Second: Lebanon fragile hold Day 26. No confirmed operational direction from Iran to Hezbollah following the July 8-9 CENTCOM strike package and Iranian counter-strikes. The Khamenei funeral period's closure removes the analytical ambiguity about whether Iran was withholding Lebanon instructions due to mourning protocols or genuine strategic recalibration. The July 11 talk resumption — which explicitly covers the MOU dispute including the Lebanon-ceasefire dimension — is the most relevant Lebanon signal: if the July 11 session produces Iran acknowledgment of Lebanon ceasefire compliance, the Lebanon fragile-hold designation could upgrade. Third: Peru — JNE formally confirmed Keiko Fujimori and vice presidents will receive credentials at the Grand National Theater in San Borja on July 15 at noon (T-4 from July 11 evening). First and Second Vice Presidents Galarreta and Torres will be formally credentialed. Inauguration remains July 28. Milei (Argentina) confirmed attendance. The Andean resource nationalism premium eliminated at Fujimori certification holds at lower-risk level in copper and silver markets. Fourth: Colombia de la Espriella T-27 to August 7 inauguration. No transition complications reported July 11. Fifth: Venezuela earthquake Day 18 — 1,719+ confirmed dead, 46,600+ missing. Maduro government continues to restrict US humanitarian access. Colombia's new government (T-27) faces immediate cross-border humanitarian pressure from Day 1 of the de la Espriella administration.

items.summary: The July 11 energy session records the commodity market's first sub-$72 close since the July 7-9 re-escalation sequence — a qualitatively different pricing signal from the July 10 de-risk-from-peak movement. WTI's consolidation below $72 on July 11 reflects Iran's return supply entering the Omani-corridor tanker stream actively rather than the war-risk premium merely retreating in response to diplomatic tone. The analytical distinction: the July 10 brief characterized $73-74 as 'partial war-risk premium trim on Qatar channel signal — not normalization confidence.' The July 11 sub-$72 level has a different character. When Iranian crude is flowing through re-opened Hormuz channels and buyers are pricing it into supply estimates, oil falls below the war-risk premium floor not because tension is decreasing but because supply is arriving. This is what the 'disinflation gateway' scenario the brief has tracked since June 19 looks like in commodity markets: not a dramatic drop, but a quiet consolidation below the premium threshold as tankers transit and buyers receive cargo. The practical consequence for Warsh's September SEP: if WTI holds below $72 through the August CPI print (due roughly September 11), the energy component of CPI will show measurable disinflation relative to the May 4.2% reading. That energy-CPI deceleration is the single most important factor in whether Warsh's September SEP can shift the median dot from 'hike' to 'hold.' The Lloyd's war-risk normalization announcement — which would unlock the 118-tanker backlog and drive Kpler's 40-transit/day projection — has not been confirmed as of July 11, but the sub-$72 WTI signal is consistent with a market that is beginning to price Lloyd's normalization as probable within days to weeks rather than uncertain. On the tariff calendar: Section 122 expires July 24 (T-13). The USTR Section 301 investigation completion deadline is July 20 (T-9, earlier than the July 24 expiry). The proposed Section 301 structure — 12.5% on 46 countries (China, Vietnam, India, Thailand, Japan, South Korea, and 40 others) and 10% on 15 others (EU, Canada, UK, Mexico, Argentina, etc.) — is the operative USTR proposal. No White House finalization announcement has been made as of July 11 evening. The structural difference from Section 122: Section 301 has NO rate cap (Section 122 caps at 15%) and NO time limit (Section 122's 150-day clock expires July 24). The post-July 20 window — if USTR completes its investigation July 20 but no White House announcement follows before July 24 — creates a potential 3-4 day tariff gap that importers are currently hedging. FERC AI pathway: 30-day informational report T-7 (July 18). The six ISO/RTO operators (MISO, SPP, PJM, NYISO, ISO-NE, CAISO) must submit their resource adequacy plans by July 18. PNW data center corridors (Quincy WA, The Dalles OR, Eastern Oregon — BPA/WECC outside the six scopes) will track the July 18 submissions as de facto national standards. Pharma 232 scheduled effective July 31 (T-20).

items.summary: Three secondary economic threads on July 11 evening. First: OBBB Law Day 12 (signed June 29, effective July 1). Medicaid work requirements and SNAP healthy food restrictions remain active in 18 states with no federal court stay issued on any OBBB title. The Aragon v. Rollins ruling's downstream signal continues to accumulate legal weight as OBBB implementation proceeds — the federal district court's June 22 invalidation of USDA food-restriction demonstration approvals in five states establishes a constraint on USDA administrative authority that will be cited in challenges to OBBB's own SNAP provisions as they take effect. No federal court has granted a stay on OBBB's Medicaid or SNAP titles as of July 11. CBO's 10-year deficit estimate ($3.4T) for OBBB remains the operative fiscal impact assessment. Second: Russia CDU-11 offline confirmation is the July 11 economic session's most significant new data point. The prior analytical framing — CDU-10 destroyed (38%), CDU-11 potentially recoverable sooner — is superseded. The CDU-11 is offline due to supporting infrastructure damage, not direct strike damage, but recovery requires infrastructure restoration that is not weeks but potentially months, bringing the CDU-11 timeline closer to the CDU-10's multi-month horizon. The combined 75% offline picture fundamentally extends the Russian domestic fuel crisis's macroeconomic inflationary pressure beyond the September FOMC decision. Warsh's deflationary impulse thesis — which required both Hormuz normalization and Russian refining recovery — now has only one of its two required conditions showing improvement (Hormuz, via sub-$72 WTI). Russian refining recovery is a multi-month story. The September FOMC's ability to characterize the dual two-source energy shock as transient is materially constrained by the CDU-11 confirmation. Third: SAVE America Reconciliation 3.0 (Speaker Johnson's post-OBBB legislative agenda: voter ID through budget reconciliation) remains in the Senate Byrd bath risk zone. Senate Republican skepticism on direct budgetary impact of voter ID mandates is publicly expressed. No new procedural steps July 11. The OBBB's law-day progression continues to dominate the domestic legislative tracking arc.

items.summary: The July 11 infrastructure session delivers the 2026 Washington fire season's most significant positive resolution to date: the Chelan Hills Fire's Day 7 ICS-209 at 95% contained, validating the extended-containment posture against the July 10 red flag test. The dozer-built line geometry that held at 50% through the atmospheric river window (Days 4-5) demonstrated structural robustness against Day 6's red flag conditions (10-20% relative humidity, wind gusts to 35mph) — the same meteorological conditions that produced the Days 1-3 zero-containment catastrophe. The 200+ personnel maintained ember suppression and perimeter integrity through the wind event. The jump from 50% (Day 6, under red flag test) to 95% (Day 7) confirms that the established dozer geometry controlled the fire's perimeter across the remaining uncontained segments as weather moderated from the red flag peak. At 95% containment, the Chelan Hills Fire is entering its mop-up and patrol phase — the operational transition from suppression to demobilization. The 5% remaining uncontained perimeter likely represents roadless or terrain-restricted sections where aerial application is the primary suppression tool. Level 3 evacuations for the Orondo/Chelan Falls corridor (~500 residents) are expected to be downgraded to Level 2 or Level 1 in the July 11-12 cycle as the containment figure validates perimeter stability. The human-caused investigation (Douglas County Sheriff Tyler Caille + state fire investigators) continues; the official ICS-209 acreage stands at ~9,861 acres. Confirmed fatality count: 1 (human remains found in burned vehicle). Structures destroyed: 100+, predominantly in McNeil Canyon. Damage estimate: $9.1 million (likely to rise in final assessment). Kartar Fire (Okanogan County, near Omak): 100% contained — a decisive resolution of what the July 10 brief characterized as the session's 'highest-priority new fire-management concern.' The Colville Reservation fire's 15% containment on Day 6 under red flag conditions was the brief's highest-risk open question on July 10; the 100% containment confirmation on July 11 eliminates it from the active threat matrix. Final acreage: 11,746 acres. The B and O Fire (near Okanogan, first reported July 9) is not yet at large-fire scale based on available reporting. It is inside the east Cascades onset region — any rapid growth under east-wind conditions warrants immediate tracking; it is the session's lowest-confidence new fire thread. Sourdough Fire (North Cascades NP, Whatcom County, Day 7): Extended attack posture confirmed with SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) confirmed open. Seattle City Light's Skagit dam hydropower supply (Gorge, Diablo, Ross dams) continues partial restoration. The Sourdough Fire is the session's only significant remaining contained-but-active threat. NIFC PL4 Day 13 (first since 2021): 38 large fires nationally (up from 37 on July 10), burning 541,000+ acres across 14 states. The increase from 37 to 38 is a one-unit increment — not a dramatic escalation — but confirms the national fire posture remains at maximum preparedness.

items.summary: Two primary domestic threads on July 11 evening. First: The measles high-consequence sub-window closes with a three-day consecutive clean streak — the July 10-11 peak window (Days 8-9 of the June 19 Lumen Field incubation timeline) has produced zero confirmed mass-event clusters in King County or Snohomish County. This is analytically the most significant epidemiological reassurance signal of the 2026 measles arc. The sub-window's epidemiological logic: Days 8-9 of incubation post-exposure represent the highest probability window for secondary transmission chains from a mass-exposure event (~69,000 attendees at the June 19 FIFA match at Lumen Field) to become clinically identifiable through Georgetown University's integrated wastewater DNA and emergency department data fusion platform. Three consecutive clean days through the peak window means either (a) the June 19 exposure did not seed sufficient community transmission chains to produce identifiable clusters, or (b) the chains are seeded but below Georgetown's detection threshold. The former scenario (option a) is substantially more likely after three peak-window clean days. The window formally closes tomorrow (July 12, Day 10). If July 12 closes clean, the brief will characterize the June 19 Lumen Field mass-event cluster risk as resolved for the primary incubation window. Note: a June 19 secondary transmission chain can produce tertiary exposures that extend beyond Day 10 — but the probability of a confirmed mass-event cluster emerging after Day 10 is substantially lower than during the peak window. National measles count: 2,231 confirmed cases as of July 9 CDC update (up from 2,170 as of July 2 — 61 new cases in one week, a modest deceleration from prior weeks). The CIDRAP slowing signal (Day 35) holds as the baseline national reassurance signal, and MMR coverage at 92.5% (below the 95% herd immunity threshold) remains the structural vulnerability. Second: FEMA compound PNW demand reduction is now decisive. The Chelan Hills Fire's 95% containment breakthrough and the Kartar Fire's 100% resolution simultaneously remove the two highest-priority PNW fire-management concerns from the July 11 active demand matrix. The compound FEMA logistics posture (Chelan Hills Level 3 evacuations + Kartar active suppression) has shifted to a single-fire managed mode (Sourdough extended attack + B and O Fire new ignition). The Level 3 evacuation downgrade for the Orondo/Chelan Falls corridor (~500 residents) is expected in the July 11-12 cycle. NIFC PL4 Day 13 and 38 national large fires maintain elevated national resource constraint, but the Washington-specific FEMA demand is now substantially reduced from July 10's posture.

items.summary: The July 11 PNW fire session is defined by two simultaneous decisive containment resolutions — the 2026 Washington fire season's most consequential positive development since the season's July 4 outbreak. Chelan Hills Fire (Day 7, Douglas County WA, between Orondo and Chelan Falls): 95% contained. The Day 6 red flag test validated the dozer-line geometry built under the atmospheric river window. The 200+ personnel held spot-fire suppression and perimeter integrity through 10-20% relative humidity and 35mph gusts — conditions identical to the Days 1-3 zero-containment catastrophe that destroyed 100+ structures in McNeil Canyon. The analytical significance of the Day 7 95% figure: the July 10 brief's central question was 'does 50% containment geometry hold under red flag conditions identical to Days 1-3?' The answer is yes, decisively. The Chelan Hills Fire is entering mop-up and patrol operations. Level 3 evacuations for the Orondo/Chelan Falls corridor are expected to be downgraded to Level 2 or Level 1 within the July 11-12 cycle. Highways 97 and 97A remain open. Human-caused investigation continues. Kartar Fire (Okanogan County, Colville Reservation, near Omak): 100% contained at 11,746 acres. This is the complete resolution of the July 10 brief's 'highest-priority new fire management concern' — a fire that had 15% containment under red flag conditions 24 hours ago. The Kartar containment closes the most acute fire-management emergency in eastern Washington's Okanogan County terrain. B and O Fire (near Okanogan, first reported July 9): Not yet at large-fire scale but inside the east Cascades onset region. The onset region (east Okanogan/Columbia Plateau) is in Day 14 of the projected onset window (June 29 - July 1 onset is now Day 14 past). Any rapid B and O growth warrants immediate tracking — Okanogan terrain presents the same suppression challenge that made the Kartar Fire the high-concern fire for three days. Sourdough Fire (Whatcom County, North Cascades NP, Day 7): Extended attack posture with SR-20 (North Cascades Highway) confirmed open and Skagit dam hydropower restoration developing. The Sourdough fire is a managed wilderness burn — ecologically within the North Cascades' natural fire regime, logistically complex due to roadless terrain but not threatening WUI communities. Seattle City Light's Gorge/Diablo/Ross hydropower supply is in partial recovery as fire proximity to the dam complex is cleared. BPA's grid demand from Western Washington has reduced with the Chelan Hills containment breakthrough — the acute WUI fire-proximity demand on BPA's east-of-Cascades tie lines is substantially reduced from July 4-10 levels. NIFC PL4 Day 13: 38 large fires, 541,000+ acres, 14 states. The one-fire increment from July 10 (37 to 38) reflects continued national fire season intensity without Washington-specific escalation.
